inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average Q2 2026 (6-K Q2-2026 line 745: 206.346 basic + 1.482 RSUs), i.e. after the January 2026 synthetic repurchase (capital repayment + reverse split, $496.7m, issued shares to 206.8m incl. 0.7m treasury). The 2027/2031/2032 convertibles (adjusted conversion prices $79.76 / $63.19 / $64.13) are out of the money and anti-dilutive; they are carried at face in total_debt. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. equity-award withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. Note: the bull-case USD IV sits near the $63-64 conversion prices, so above that level net-share settlement would add modest dilution not modelled here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash-flow statement: share-based compensation $50.4m + tax withholding on vesting of stock awards (financing) $27.27m = $77.67m. QIAGEN's adjusted measures do not publish a combined SBC-incl-withholding figure, so the two lines are summed. H1 2026: $16.6m + $13.9m (SBC lower on PSU achievement re-estimate and CEO-departure forfeiture reversal - not treated as a run-rate).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 synthetic repurchase $280.1m (Jan 2025); a further $496.7m in Jan 2026. Dividend initiated 2025 ($54.2m), $0.35/sh ($72.3m) declared Q2 2026 and paid July 2026. QIAGEN is an active repurchaser, so the flat share count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are USD (20-F / 6-K, US GAAP). Priced against the Frankfurt/XETRA quote QIA.DE in EUR. fx_rate converts model USD -> quote EUR = 1 / EURUSD 1.1204 (Yahoo EURUSD=X, 2026-10-23T21:29Z) = 0.892538 EUR per USD. Parity check against the NYSE listing QGEN (USD 50.39 at the 2026-10-23 NYSE close): 45.05 EUR x 1.1204 = USD 50.47, a 0.17% tie, which confirms rate, direction and that one QIA.DE share = one QGEN share. USD values are emitted as *_usd twins; unsuffixed values are EUR so they compare directly to current_price. refresh_price.py does not move fx_rate - refresh it with the price.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:51Z (XETRA, after the 17:30 CEST close - effectively the Friday regular close); Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: US 10y risk-free ~4.2%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 (defensive consumables-led diagnostics with a cyclical instrument/life-sciences tail) -> cost of equity ~8.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3% (mostly low/zero-coupon convertibles and Schuldschein), ~2.4% after tax, at ~13% debt weight on a ~$10.5bn market cap -> ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. No ad-hoc premium for the QuantiFERON policy exposure or the 2026 guidance cut: that risk is carried in the flows through the 25% bear weight (owner-fcf-adaptations (f), charge risk once). Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP filer: operating lease cost is straight-line opex already inside GAAP operating income, hence inside the EBITDA margin path (treatment B). Operating lease liabilities ($28.8m current + $129.1m long-term at FY2025) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; lease_cost_pct_path is 0 because the charge is already in EBITDA. One treatment, consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests; flows are attributable as reported.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build), routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US' - QIAGEN is a profitable, cash-generative consumables-led molecular diagnostics / life-sciences tools company (>85% recurring revenue), so owner FCF is the right stream; owner-fcf-adaptations.md applied for the USD-statement / EUR-quote split and the lease rule. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF). BASE: EBITDA margin path is GAAP EBITDA (operating income + D&A, so interest income and expense are excluded and the build is unlevered) PLUS SBC added back so the engine can charge SBC explicitly: FY2025 (465.9 + 193.7 + 50.4) / 2,090 = 34.0%. GAAP rather than adjusted EBITDA because QIAGEN's restructuring/integration charges recur most years. NET DEBT: total debt $1,643.6m less cash $768.5m and short-term investments $25.0m at 2026-06-30 (6-K Q2-2026 lines 38/59/64/1052). Net debt company, so interest income ($59m FY2025, $19.9m H1 2026) is NOT stripped from last_fcf (rule applies only to material net cash); the projections are unlevered anyway. EQUITY BRIDGE: the June 30 balance sheet already contains H1 2026 owner FCF while projection year 1 is the full FY2026, so H1 2026 owner FCF is deducted once; and the $72.3m dividend declared at June 30 but paid in July is deducted. CASH TAX: FY2024-25 cash taxes were abnormally low ($15.7m / $17.3m, ~3.5% of FY2025 pretax, with German/Spanish/UK refunds); FY2023 was $82.4m (~19%). GAAP ETR 13.3% FY2025 vs 25.8% Dutch statutory; Pillar Two 15% minimum applies. Cash rate ramps 12% -> 20%. No Q3 2026 results are in the extracted filings (QIAGEN normally reports late Oct / early Nov); the share price rose ~9% in the week to 2026-10-23, so check the Q3 print before acting.

equity_bridge.item: H1 2026 owner FCF already in the 2026-06-30 cash balance (OCF 301.3 - PP&E capex 89.8 - SBC 16.6 - award withholding taxes 13.9); FY2026 is projected in full, so remove the half already banked
Dividend $0.35/sh declared Q2 2026, paid July 2026 (still in June cash)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.2% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 2.2% and EPS 5yr 4.9% - divergence >30%. Every 3- and 5-year window is distorted by the COVID testing boom (FY2021 revenue 2,252 peak) and the 2024 NeuMoDx exit impairment (FY2024 EPS 0.37), and book equity is shrunk by ~$1.1bn of synthetic repurchases since 2024. The 10-year revenue CAGR (5.0%) straddles the cycle and sits just under management's ~7% CER 2024-2028 target, so it is the anchor used.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - award withholding taxes; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 270.3, FY2022 511.1, FY2023 244.9, FY2024 428.6, FY2025 375.6. The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-9.8%) is below reported (-8.2%) because SBC plus award withholding rose from $74.9m (FY2022) to $77.7m while FCF fell - a modest, not structural, gap.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026 at the reaffirmed ~1-2% CER guide plus a small FX tailwind (H1 reported +1.1%); 2027-28 re-accelerate as discontinued-product headwinds lapse, QuantiFERON rebases and pillars grow ~9% - still short of the ~7% 2024-28 CAGR target, which the 2026 cut made back-end-loaded; fade to 3% by year 9.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: FY2025 34.0% (GAAP EBITDA + SBC); H1 2026 32.6% incl. a $15.2m non-cash software abandonment (33.9% ex). Guidance: adjusted operating margin steady in 2026 absorbing ~160bp of Parse/tariff/FX pressure, >=31% by 2028 (+150bp vs 2025). Base captures ~150bp by FY2028 and ~200bp at maturity.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: PP&E + intangibles purchases: 7.6% FY2023, 8.5% FY2024, 9.9% FY2025 (capacity + SAP upgrade), 8.9% H1 2026. Normalises to 8%, roughly matching D&A at maturity.
base.wc_capture_pct_rationale: Manufacturer/distributor with receivables + inventory well above payables; H1 2026 inventory build. Growth consumes cash: -15% of the revenue increase.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_rationale: Cash taxes FY2024-25 ~$16-17m (refund-driven, ~3.5% of pretax); FY2023 ~19%; adjusted tax rate ~19-20%; Pillar Two 15% floor. Ramp 12% -> 20% on EBIT by FY2029.

scenario_narratives.base: QuantiFERON's 2026 immigration-testing hit proves a one-off rebasing: the franchise holds ~$500m in 2026 and resumes mid-single-digit growth as TST-to-blood conversion continues. Discontinued-product headwinds lapse from mid-2026, QIAstat-Dx and QIAcuity keep compounding and Parse adds single-cell revenue, so group growth recovers to 5-6% in 2027-28 - below the 7% Capital Markets Day CAGR, which the 2026 cut has made unreachable on schedule. The US life-sciences instrument cycle stays soft but stops worsening. Margins recover ~150bp by 2028 as tariffs are absorbed and Parse scales, short of the full >=31% adjusted-margin target. Cash taxes normalise from refund-flattered levels to ~20%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Both cyclical drags turn together: US/Middle East immigration screening normalises and latent-TB testing broadens into occupational and high-risk-population screening, while NIH/biopharma capex recovers and lifts QIAcuity and automation (QIAsymphony/QIAsprint Connect) placements and their consumable pull-through. Pillars reach ~$2bn in 2028, QDI's AI/NVIDIA work earns higher-margin software revenue, and QIAGEN hits its ~7% growth / >=31% adjusted margin path a year late, reaching 37.5% pre-SBC EBITDA. Requires several independent things to go right, which is why its weight is held at 25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The guidance cut is the first sign of a structural slowdown, not a blip: immigration-testing policy keeps QuantiFERON flat for years, academic/government funding cuts keep instrument placements depressed, and BioFire (bioMerieux) and Cepheid (Danaher) out-scale QIAstat-Dx in syndromic testing. Tariffs and FX keep gross margin at ~66% and sub-scale R&D/M&A spend has to rise just to defend position, so pre-SBC EBITDA margin slips to 32.5% and growth settles at 2.5-3%. Capital returns continue but the business is valued as a slow-growing consumables franchise at a 15x terminal cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because management cut FY2026 guidance (>=5% to ~1-2% CER) within three months of issuing it, and QuantiFERON (~24% of sales) depends on immigration policy outside the company's control. Base held at 50%: Q2 2026 beat the cut guide and >85% recurring consumables revenue limits downside. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs both the immigration-testing recovery and a US life-sciences capex recovery, two independent events.

valuation_philosophy.summary: QIAGEN is valued as a mature, consumables-led diagnostics compounder on a strict owner-FCF basis: SBC plus the cash taxes withheld on award vesting are charged as real costs and the share count is held flat (repurchases fund it). The flows are USD and discounted at a USD-built 8.5% WACC; per-share values are converted to EUR at the dated EURUSD rate for comparison with the XETRA quote, with the NYSE QGEN listing as the parity check. Guidance-year growth is anchored to the reaffirmed 1-2% CER outlook; margin and growth recovery thereafter are deliberately short of the 2028 Capital Markets Day targets after the 2026 cut.
key_risks_to_valuation: QuantiFERON immigration-testing demand: a second policy shock would move the base toward the bear growth path.
US life-sciences/academic capital spending: instrument placements drive consumable pull-through across PCR, NGS and Sample technologies.
Cash tax normalisation: FY2024-25 cash taxes were refund-flattered; a faster move to 20%+ lowers near-term FCF, slower raises it.
Margin recovery: tariffs and FX have already cost ~120bp; the base assumes ~150bp of recovery by 2028.
FX: the EUR value moves one-for-one with EURUSD; fx_rate is not updated by price-only refreshes.
Q3 2026 results (due late Oct / early Nov 2026) are not yet in the extracted filings; the shares rose ~9% in the week to 2026-10-23.
